reason: The text shows the Israelite people responding obediently to Barak's military summons (וַיַּזְעֵק בָּרָק אֶת־ זְבוּלֻן וְאֶת־ נַפְתָּלִי) and following him into battle with 10,000 men. The people willingly assemble and fight under his command. While Barak demonstrates hesitation or lack of confidence—requiring Deborah to accompany him before he will lead—this is a character trait of the leader himself, not antagonism from the people toward their leader. The narrative shows voluntary compliance and successful military cooperation between leader and followers, not antagonism.
